podcast.body: Originally recorded in 1966, this song was one of three early hit singles for Neil Diamond on the Bang Record label. Initially, it struggled to get airplay in the States but eventually became a big hit in California. Diamond recounted pulling over in Toronto to listen when it came on the radio, feeling it was "the fulfillment of everything I ever wanted." Thirty-five years later, after four years of Freudian analysis, he realized he had written it about himself, as reflected in the autobiographical lyrics about seeking a partner who won't play games. "I was in Toronto and Solitary man had just been released. Nobody would play it in the States. But finally, it was played and became a big hit in California."
